correctness.rationale: For a fixed read prefix, endpoint counts \((p,q)\) obey four exhaustive transitions: \(0:(p,0)\), \(1:(p+q,p)\), \(2:(q,p+q)\), \(3:(0,q)\). Writing \(S=p+q\), \(M=\max\{p,q\}\), induction proves \(S\le F_{j+3}\), \(M\le F_{j+2}\). Equality forces the same choice, \(1\) or \(2\), at every step, yielding precisely the two claimed extremizers. Independent brute-force reconstruction through \(n=19\) and dynamic fiber counting agree and terminate with VERIFY_OK.

The Hulett--Chandak--Wootters abstraction uses unit shifts and is not a stronger theorem for the shifted \((3,2)\) multiplicity problem.

value.rationale: Maximum fiber size is the natural worst-case list size of a deterministic many-to-one read channel. The result gives an exact formula for every admissible blocklength and uniquely identifies the two most ambiguous outputs, quantifying a channel feature that capacity does not measure. The \((3,2)\) case is the first nontrivial odd-window example singled out in the primary literature, so this is a structurally motivated invariant rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
